description: Discriminator: does a 70000-byte command value survive the real marshal/unmarshal pair, or does the decoder recover a shorter value and leave bytes in the stream? Prefix: the harness builds the command, marshals it with the implementation's own codec and then unmarshals from the same buffer. Controls: the events print the declared length, the wire length, the decoded length and how many bytes the decoder consumed.

harness.description: In-package Go test that round-trips one oversized command value through the real codec and reports the decoded length and consumed bytes.
semantic_changes: harness-only scaffolding: no replica is constructed; the test calls the state codec directly
the harness wraps the already-buffered wire bytes in a fresh reader, which is what the unmarshal expects

legality.derivation: The value built is one the client's configured command size permits to be constructed, and both codec directions are the implementation's own.
legality.applicability: One command, one value, no replica.
unresolved: the client's own allocation cap was not read

grounding.derivation: The event reports the decoded length, whether the bytes match and how much of the wire the decoder consumed, which are the observable consequences of the length field.
grounding.applicability: The command was marshalled and then unmarshalled.

observable_properties.description: A command value that the client can build must survive the codec unchanged.

uncertainties: the check does not exercise a replica reader or the client's allocation, so the desync's effect on a follow-on message is not observed
the shipped configuration's 1000-byte commands are inside the field's range
